--- title: connection description: API Reference for the connection function. --- The `connection()` function allows you to indicate rendering should wait for an incoming user request before continuing. It's useful when a component doesn't use [Request-time APIs](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) like `cookies` or `headers`, but still needs to produce different output per request, such as `Math.random()` or `new Date()`. ```ts filename="app/page.tsx" switcher import { connection } from 'next/server' export default async function Page() { await connection() // prerendering stops here // the following code only runs at request time const rand = Math.random() return {rand} } ``` ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher import { connection } from 'next/server' export default async function Page() { await connection() // prerendering stops here // the following code only runs at request time const rand = Math.random() return {rand} } ``` ## Examples ### Synchronous database drivers Queries from synchronous database drivers like `better-sqlite3` complete during prerendering. If you are not already using Request-time APIs, call `connection()` before your query to exclude them from prerendering: ```ts filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher import { connection } from 'next/server' import Database from 'better-sqlite3' const db = new Database('app.db') export async function getVisitorCount() { await connection() return db.prepare('SELECT value FROM counters WHERE name = ?').get('visitors') } ``` ```js filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher import { connection } from 'next/server' import Database from 'better-sqlite3' const db = new Database('app.db') export async function getVisitorCount() { await connection() return db.prepare('SELECT value FROM counters WHERE name = ?').get('visitors') } ``` Now any component that calls `getVisitorCount()` will be excluded from prerendering, along with the rest of its output. ## Reference ### Type ```jsx function connection(): Promise ``` ### Parameters - The function does not accept any parameters. ### Returns - The function returns a `void` Promise. It is not meant to be consumed. ## Good to know - `connection` replaces [`unstable_noStore`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unstable_noStore) to better align with the future of Next.js. - The function is only necessary when dynamic rendering is required and common Request-time APIs are not used. - With [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), place the component that calls `connection()` inside a [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary, either directly or through an ancestor such as a [`loading.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading) file. The nearest boundary's fallback is prerendered into the [static shell](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell), and the code after `connection()` runs at request time. item.text:
The welcome page now schedules a `page_view` POST with Next.js `after()`, so analytics delivery does not hold up the response. It uses `connection()` to run the callback for each request rather than at build time.

Set `ANALYTICS_ENDPOINT` to a service that accepts `{"event":"page_view","path":"/"}`. An optional bearer token is supported through `ANALYTICS_API_KEY`; see [.env.example](/workspace/.env.example). The implementation is in [app/page.tsx](/workspace/app/page.tsx) and [app/analytics.ts](/workspace/app/analytics.ts).

The build and TypeScript check passed. In a live check, the page returned in 217 ms while a deliberately delayed analytics endpoint completed after 900 ms and received the event.
